claims.claim: Commercial driverless authorization requirements became enforceable May 28, 2026, with implemented public complaints confirmed June 2.
claims.qualification: September 1, 2025 statutory effectiveness differs from compliance after implementing rules.
claims.recheck: Governing law or agency implementation change

claims.claim: Commercial authorization concerns passenger/property transport furthering a commercial enterprise on public highways/streets without a human driver.
claims.qualification: Classify the actual vehicle, engaged feature, purpose and human role; do not infer from a brand label.

claims.claim: Authorization is nonexpiring but material information must be updated within 30 days, with separate document and safety enforcement paths.
claims.qualification: The 30-day information deadline is not a universal safety cure period.
claims.recheck: Material supplier record or controlling requirements change

claims.claim: Current public lookup is TxMCCS Truck Stop; prior /automated-vehicles/operators renders 404.
claims.qualification: No exhaustive holder/vehicle audit or census performed.

claims.claim: DPS publishes platform-specific responder plans; a catalog entry alone is not booking or current authorization evidence.
claims.qualification: Use the plan for the actual vehicle, not merely the company name.

claims.claim: Pilot preparedness is $5,500; one 60-load replacement week adds $7,200; combined incremental stress cost $12,700 above common $324,000 freight.
claims.qualification: All rates, hours, loads and interruption inputs invented for an editable commercial comparison; no frequency or quote inferred.
claims.recheck: Actual staffing, contract, service or replacement evidence
